Subject: Renewal redlines and capacity uplift — proposed edits

Hi Maya,

Thanks again for the productive call yesterday. Per our discussion I'm attaching a first-pass consolidation of the renewal paperwork with the proposed capacity uplift and term language. Key asks for your review:

- Term: Redwood proposes moving to an 18-month renewal term (was 12). We can discuss 24 as an option if pricing tiers align.
- Capacity: Add 150k extra inference hours per month as Exhibit A; pricing shown on tab "Uplift".
- SLA credits: language in Section 6 — please flag any internal approval constraints.

Attachments: HeronAI_Renewal_Draft_v1.docx (redline enabled).

Could you confirm the expected sign-off path on your side (legal + procurement), and whether you need a separate side-letter for data residency? I copied our legal lead Laura and Ben in sales ops to keep them in the loop.

If you prefer, we can schedule 30 minutes tomorrow to walk the redlines live.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Maya Singh <maya@heron.ai>

Cc: contracts@heron.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-02T12:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal redlines and capacity uplift — proposed edits

Hi Karthik —

Thanks for the draft. A few immediate notes from contracts: we like the 18-month compromise but our procurement team wants:

1) SLA credit cap not to exceed 5% of monthly fees (Section 6 currently open).
2) Data retention and residency: we need an explicit clause stating that customer data for Heron AI EU workloads will be kept in the APAC/EU region and not be replicated outside without prior consent.
3) Billing/proration: If the uplift starts mid-billing-cycle, we need proration language on Exhibit A.

I've attached our redlines (Heron_Redlines_v1.pdf) with in-line comments. Procurement will need to see the final numbers before approving the 150k uplift.

Question: do you have an internal playbook for how credits are calculated? That will help speed review.

Regards,
Maya Singh
Head of Procurement, Heron AI
attachments: Heron_Redlines_v1.pdf

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-03T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal redlines and capacity uplift — legal notes

Karthik / Ben —

I reviewed Maya's redlines and the draft. High-level legal input:

- Section 6 (SLA): can accept a 5% cap on credits but we should insert a "sole and exclusive remedy" sentence to limit exposure (see suggested language in attached file).
- Data residency: propose adding an Exhibit describing region-specific data handling and an approval process for cross-border transfers. That keeps the MSA clean while addressing procurement's ask.
- Billing / proration: recommend explicit formula for mid-cycle adjustments (simple days-prorated calculation).

I've attached a short snippet with suggested language (MSA_section6_suggestion.txt). Also recommend we route final redline through Finance for confirmation on the revenue recognition / proration impact.

If you want, I can draft the final redline to send back to Heron so we don't bounce versions.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference

Hi Maya —

Looping Marissa from Finance so we can confirm proration and the order-form spreadsheet. Per Laura's note, legal is comfortable with 5% SLA cap as long as we add the "sole and exclusive remedy" language. Laura — would you be able to produce the consolidated redline by Friday?

Proposed compromise from our side: 18-month term (instead of 12 or 24) with the 150k uplift effective at start of next billing period. Marissa, can you confirm impact on startup proration if effective mid-cycle?

Next steps: if we can align on language today/Friday, I'll issue a DocuSign envelope with the updated Exhibit A and MSA redline for counter-signature. Attached the current order-form workbook for your review.

Attachments: OrderForm_ExhibitA_2028-04-04.xlsx

Karthik
